fields.title: Design for scale-out and tenant isolation first
fields.statement: Treat data distribution as a first-class, day-one concern — never a feature bolted on later — in both of its forms: scale-out (sharding a large data set across servers) and tenant isolation (a distinct database store per cloud tenant). Both share the same machinery: make querying a shard set as simple as querying a single database, provide a global record identity (the ShardKey virtual compound key) where the engine no longer enforces one, and let applications be explicit about read vs. write connections from the start.
fields.rationale: Neither form can be retrofitted: sharding forces a careful rethink of the data model and data access (unique/foreign-key guarantees no longer come from the engine), and tenant isolation must be structural — a database boundary, not a WHERE clause — to reliably prevent cross-tenant query results and to enable per-tenant backups, SLAs, replication, and clean decommissioning. Scale-out underwrites cost-effective growth, active/active disaster recovery, regional latency, and data-residency compliance; tenanting underwrites consolidated infrastructure with per-customer guarantees, including multi-tenant Orleans behind a single cluster. ArgentSea exists precisely because it is the only .NET framework built for this — so being explicit about topology and read/write today makes later scaling a configuration change rather than a rewrite.

metadata.provenanceNote: Derived from ArgentSea.DocFx during initial agentic onboarding, 2026-07-19. Reframed same day per operator direction: tenanting elevated to equal footing with scale-out (structural isolation, per-tenant data management, multi-tenant Orleans). Draft for operator review.
